title: Warn when another session is already working here, and let a narrowed sprint be renamed

history.detail:
PASS: PASS — round 1. Audited 1d7be4c, main checkout. Sprint file read fresh.

================================================================
THE ENV-VAR QUESTION — CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY, AND MORE STRONGLY THAN DEV TEAM COULD
================================================================

You asked for a second look at whether CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID/CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT are genuinely Claude-Code-provided rather than something this framework sets, on the grounds that it is load-bearing for Req 2. I am in a position to answer that better than a grep can, because I am myself a Claude Code session:

    CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT=qa1
    CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=6f40f6d7-7669-5fd2-a92b-6d69e72ba681

Both set, in my own environment, in a session this framework did not launch. CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT reads `qa1` — my actual role, which corroborates your finding that it matches the agent a session was started with, from a session you did not run. And the session id matches the transcript path this session is recorded at, so it is a real Claude Code identifier rather than anything synthesised.

Your grep also holds when widened: no assignment to either variable anywhere in scripts/ or .claude/. The single non-read occurrence is smoke_test.sh:1215, which sets them deliberately as test fixtures — correct and expected.

Established by running, and by running somewhere neither of us controlled.

================================================================
REQ 1 — NEVER GATES. FAIL TRIGGER NOT TRIPPED.
================================================================

Three consecutive launches of the same role in one tree, with a fake claude:
    launch 1: exit=0  warned  child ran
    launch 2: exit=0  warned  child ran
    launch 3: exit=0  warned  child ran
Every launch exits 0 and the child actually executed — I checked for the child's own output rather than inferring from the absence of an error. Two sessions of one role remain possible, which is the FAIL condition avoided.

Corroborated at the code level: recordRoleClaim's read and write are both wrapped in try/catch returning safe defaults, and there is no throw path that could reach a caller. Best-effort by construction, not by intention.

REQ 1 / REQ 3 — THE BLIND SPOT IS NAMED, IN THE MESSAGE ITSELF. Read cold:

  "...this record only sees launches that went through this script, and only at the moment of launch,
   so a session started another way, or a collision that began mid-build with no new launch, is
   invisible to it. Silence never means 'nobody else is working here.' Launching anyway -- this never
   blocks."

The criterion's exact test is whether a reader could take silence as "nobody else is working here." The message answers that in those words. It also declines to presume the collision is a problem ("may be exactly what you intended... or a genuine collision"), names the earlier session and start time so the reader can check, and states the never-blocks property inline.

This is the fifth chance the sprint file mentions for a comment in this project to get an honesty claim right first time. It is right first time, and it is right in the user-facing text rather than only in a docstring, which is where it actually has to be.

================================================================
REQ 4 — ALL THREE MOVE, THE ORIGINAL SURVIVES, AND THE HASH QUESTION IS ANSWERED WHERE IT MATTERS
================================================================

Ran it rather than reading it. After renaming "Original broad title" to "Narrowed title":
    filename          sprint-1_narrowed-title.md
    frontmatter       title: "Narrowed title"
    registry title    Narrowed title
    registry file     docs/sprints/2-in-progress/sprint-1_narrowed-title.md
    original_title    Original broad title
All three move together and the registry file pointer moves with the file, which is the one that would otherwise strand /sprint-status.

Renamed a second time, to "Narrower still": original_title still reads "Original broad title", not the intermediate one. That is the specific thing the requirement asked for and the easy thing to get wrong.

THE HASH BEHAVIOUR — TESTED, AND THE REFUSAL IS EXPLICABLE, WHICH IS THE CRITERION'S REAL CONCERN. I recorded a QA1 PASS, renamed, then ran dev-done: it refuses, with the generic "sprint file has changed since QA1's PASS" message. On its own that is exactly the refusal the criterion feared nobody could explain — a rename is not an amendment of requirements, and that message says requirements may have been amended.

What makes it explicable is that the rename command says so at the moment you rename, not later at the confusing symptom:
  "Phase, verdicts, hashes and history are untouched. If this sprint already has a recorded QA1 PASS,
   the sprint file's content just changed (the title/original_title lines did) -- the next
   /sprint-dev-done will correctly ask for a fresh /sprint-qa1 look first... This is expected, not a
   bug."
The explanation is delivered where the cause is, which is the right placement and the same principle sprint 27's own Finding A is about. Decided behaviour, tested, and explained in advance rather than diagnosed after.

================================================================
THINGS I WENT LOOKING FOR AND DID NOT FIND
================================================================

The test-only path override is production code carrying a test affordance, so I checked it. It is documented as exactly that, checked first, and correctly noted as "a real launch never sets it." If a production caller did set it, the only consequence is the claim landing elsewhere and the warning degrading to silence — bounded, and silence already means nothing by this feature's own design. Acceptable.

I also checked whether the runtime claims file leaks — a record of session ids and timestamps would be precisely the sprint 22 class. It does not: `.claude/role-claims.json` is named in BOTH .gitignore and .npmignore, each with a comment explaining why, and the only packed path matching "role-claims" is `scripts/launcher/role-claims.js`, the module itself. No claims file exists in this repo's tree either. That is sprint 22's lesson applied pre-emptively rather than found by a later sweep. (My first check reported it packed — that was my own substring match hitting the .js filename, not a real finding. Recording that because I nearly reported it as one.)

REQ 5 / REQ 6 — package.json 0.1.29, one line. ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED; ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, 190 OK (up 9, matching the 7 unit and 2 CLI integration tests); verify-tarball.sh PASSED, "Installed 0.1.29 (first install)".

The two problems found and fixed mid-build are both real and both fixed in the right shape: the claims-file test pollution solved centrally in runRoleCli() so no individual test needed touching, and the pre-existing state-diff invariant extended to exclude last_claim the same way history already was, rather than weakened. Neither was papered over and both are the kind that would have shown up later as an unexplained flaky test.

INFORMATIONAL, CARRIED: every allowlist entry other than git and npm remains inferred; the empty-string ownedRepository declaration still falls through silently.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 25, then Pipeman ships and publishes 0.1.29, then `verify-publish 25`.

One note for whoever renames a sprint that already has a QA1 PASS: the refusal at dev-done is correct and the rename command warns you about it first. If you hit it without having read that warning, it is not a bug and re-running /sprint-qa1 is the whole recovery path.
commit=1d7be4c | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 1d7be4c380386c6e283a8309b2d509a527d84069 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS — round 1. Live-tested published npm 0.1.29 in a scratch repo. Environment: macOS Darwin arm64, claude 2.1.266. 2026-09-09. ~$0.12 in billed runs (one real session, needed to make criterion 3 honest).

PROVENANCE
0.1.29 on the registry; dist-tags.latest 0.1.29 (correct forward move); gitHead 1d7be4c380386c6e283a8309b2d509a527d84069 == last_shipped_commit; zero `reshipped` events. Content check per sprint 13's rule: all 60 published files byte-identical to `git show 1d7be4c:<path>`, MISMATCHED 0, tarball sha1 matches the registry's dist.shasum.

================================================================
CRITERION — REPRODUCE THE REPORTED COLLISION: PASS
================================================================
Launched the same role twice in one tree from a published install.

  First launch:  no collision warning. Correct — there was nothing to collide with, and a warning
                 here would be the noise that trains people to ignore it.
  Second launch: "NOTE: another QA1 session was recorded starting at 2026-09-09T04:55:58.119Z in this
                 same tree (session 2959b613-5f1f-4b48-8c07-2fed66b5e73e)... Launching anyway -- this
                 never blocks."
                 exit 0, and the launch proceeded (the spawned process ran).

It warns, it names the first session specifically — by UUID and by start timestamp, not just "another session exists" — and it does not block. All three halves of the criterion.

The record itself (`.claude/role-claims.json`) holds the *current* launch's id after each launch, so the warning reports the one before it. That is the right shape: a claim file that accumulated every launch would need pruning and would go stale silently; one that holds the last launch answers exactly the question being asked.

Worth noting where this check sits: `recordRoleClaim()` runs before `claudeOnPath()`, so the warning fires on every launch attempt regardless of whether claude is even installed. That also made this criterion testable without billing a real session, which is a side effect of a good ordering decision rather than the reason for it.

================================================================
CRITERION — THE BLIND SPOT IS REAL AND STATED: PASS. TESTED WITH A REAL SESSION.
================================================================
This is the criterion the message must not overstate, so I tested it with a genuine claude session rather than a stub — a stub would have left the objection "that wasn't really a session" open, and the whole point is what the record can and cannot see.

  claims record before:  {'qa1': '3848f0e3'}
  started a REAL claude session directly, not through run-role.js:
      it ran (result "OK"), session_id 21c09653, cost $0.12
  claims record after:   {'qa1': '3848f0e3'}   — UNCHANGED

So a session started outside the launcher is genuinely invisible to the record. Then, launching through the launcher again:
  the warning named only the previous LAUNCHER launch (2026-09-09T04:55:58.380Z)
  mentions of the outside session's id (21c09653): 0

It does not claim to have seen what it did not see. And the message says so itself, in the text a person actually reads rather than only in a comment:
  "...this record only sees launches that went through this script, and only at the moment of launch,
   so a session started another way, or a collision that began mid-build with no new launch, is
   invisible to it. Silence never means "nobody else is working here." Launching anyway -- this
   never blocks."

That penultimate sentence is the one that matters. A warning that fires on a real collision and stays silent on an invisible one is worse than no warning if silence gets read as safety — and this message forecloses that reading in the same breath as the warning. Naming a limitation in the user-facing string, not just in a code comment, is the difference between a documented blind spot and a discovered one.

================================================================
CRITERION — RENAME A SPRINT END TO END: PASS
================================================================
Renamed via the documented `--title-file` path, using a working-directory-relative file per the command file's own sprint-14 guidance ("Always a path inside your working directory, never `/tmp`" — that lesson carried into a command file written eleven sprints later, which is the framework citing its own history correctly).

  Sprint 1 renamed: "Collision probe" -> "Collision probe, narrowed to one role".

Afterwards, all four representations agree — checked independently rather than taking the success message:
  registry title      == frontmatter title == state title
  registry file path  == the file actually on disk (renamed, not orphaned)
  registry file exists on disk: True
  phase / verdicts / rounds: unchanged (dev_build, None, None, 0/0)

ORIGINAL TITLE, ACROSS TWO RENAMES. The command file says `original_title` is "set once, on the first rename". I tested the second rename specifically, because "set once" is the kind of claim that silently becomes "set every time":
  after rename 1: original_title = "Collision probe"
  after rename 2 (title now "Collision probe, narrowed twice"): original_title = "Collision probe"
Still the first title, not the intermediate one. A sprint that narrowed twice shows what it started as, which is the point.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN METHOD, twice over in this criterion. I first invoked `rename 1 "New title"` positionally and got a usage error — the command takes `--title` or `--title-file`, and that was my misreading, not a defect. Then I looked for `original_title` in the state file, found `None`, and briefly had a candidate finding; it lives in the registry and the frontmatter, where it belongs (it is a property of the sprint's identity, not of its lifecycle state). Both were mine, both caught before reaching a verdict.

================================================================
A SELF-CLAIM THE TOOL MAKES, CHECKED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED
================================================================
The rename's own output volunteers a consequence:
  "If this sprint already has a recorded QA1 PASS, the sprint file's content just changed (the
   title/original_title lines did) -- the next /sprint-dev-done will correctly ask for a fresh
   /sprint-qa1 look first... This is expected, not a bug."

That is a testable claim about an interaction with the sprint-13 hash gate, so I tested it: recorded a QA1 PASS, confirmed `dev-done` worked, re-audited, renamed, then ran `dev-done` again —
  "ERROR: Sprint 2's sprint file has changed since QA1's PASS (round 2), requirements may have been
   amended after the audit. Run /sprint-qa1 again against the current file before marking dev work
   done. No override, re-audit is the only path past this."

The rename does not quietly invalidate an audit, and it does not quietly preserve one either — it trips the existing gate, and the rename command warns you in advance that it will. Predicting your own side effect and being right about it is a better result than not having the side effect.

================================================================
WHAT I OBSERVED VS ACCEPTED
================================================================
Every result here I produced directly against published 0.1.29 in a scratch repository. The collision, the blind spot, and the rename were each observed rather than read out of the source; the one place a stub would have weakened the evidence (criterion 3) I spent real money to avoid. The tool's own success messages were checked against the registry, the frontmatter, the filesystem and the state file separately rather than trusted.

================================================================
RECOMMENDATION
================================================================
Ship-ready. The collision warning fires on the case it was built for, names the specific session it collided with, never blocks, and — the part that makes it trustworthy rather than merely present — states its own blind spot in the message a person actually reads. The rename keeps four representations in sync, preserves the original title across repeated renames, leaves the lifecycle state alone, and correctly trips the audit-hash gate while telling you in advance that it will.

Nothing carries forward as a defect. The only notes on this sprint are two corrections to my own method, recorded above so the "candidate finding" I briefly had on `original_title` is not mistaken for a real one by anyone reading the raw session.

This PASS means the code is ready, not that anyone is authorized to close sprint 25.
